evidence.mechanism: shot-02s: ochre and rust diagonals already split around the marker at the left; by shot-08s the marker sits at midspan and the bars beneath it switch colour as their force changes sign, with no caption needed.
evidence.ambition: shot-20s: a second layer appears, a load-position by diagonal strip of ochre and rust columns under the truss; still one flat 2D canvas with line-drawn members, so the rendering ideas stay few.
evidence.craft: shot-08s: cream, ochre and rust sit cleanly on the ground with no hard artefacts; the glow strokes around the marker stack and look smeared at full size, and the top third of the frame is empty.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: per-member force colour on a Warren truss has no counterpart among the anchors shown; the influence strip at shot-20s gives a composition none of them use.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: marker and load already read at the left, but the truss rides high in frame; by shot-20s the strip resolves into a settled pattern unlike the 2s frame, though the truss is small.

pairwise_justification: No archive yet: the median block is NONE, so there is no median piece to compare against head to head.

critique.change: Add a second rendering layer to the truss itself: shade each member by its force magnitude as well as sign, so the bars carry depth and load intensity instead of one flat stroke per diagonal.
Scale the truss to fill the 1280x720 frame at 2s and centre it vertically, and give the influence strip at 20s a larger share of the frame so the end state is not a small truss in empty space.
Draw the highlight around the marker's diagonals once with alpha instead of stacking translucent strokes, so the glow at shot-08s stops doubling up and looking smeared at full size.
